claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances. Let me start with the basics:

Do you have any children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do. I have a son, Alex, who's 18. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information about Alex. To determine if you can claim Child Benefit for your 18-year-old son, I need to understand his current situation.

Is Alex currently in approved education or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. He's still in college doing his A-levels.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Since Alex is 18 and in education, I need a bit more detail about his studies.

When did Alex turn 18, or when will he turn 18?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He turned 18 a few months ago, back in September.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To continue assessing eligibility, I need to know:

Is Alex enrolled in full-time, non-advanced education (such as A-levels, which are typically considered non-advanced)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right. He's doing full-time A-levels at the local sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's very helpful. Now I need to understand a bit more about your connection to Alex and your living situation:

Do you live in the UK, and is Alex living with you or are you responsible for him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

Are you or your partner currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else claimed Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody is currently claiming Child Benefit for him. That's why I'm asking about it now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. One final question:

When does Alex's current course end? Specifically, what date does his A-level course finish?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: His A-levels finish in June next year, so around late June 2025 when he takes his final exams.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! **You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

Even though Alex is 18, you can continue to receive Child Benefit for him because he is in full-time, non-advanced education (A-levels). Under UK Child Benefit rules, you can claim for young people aged 16-19 who are in approved education or training.

**Important information:**
- Your Child Benefit for Alex will continue until he finishes his A-level course in late June 2025, or until he turns 20, whichever comes first
- If Alex leaves education before completing his course, you'll need to inform HMRC as your entitlement would stop
- You should apply for Child Benefit as soon as possible, as you can only backdate claims for up to 3 months

You can apply for Child Benefit online or by post using the appropriate claim form. Make sure to have Alex's birth certificate and your bank details ready when you apply.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about your Child Benefit claim?

The benefit will continue until the earlier of: when Alex turns 20, when he leaves education, or the end of his course (late June 2025). The claimant lives in the UK, Alex lives with them, and nobody else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, so there are no conflicts.
